question: U.S. fuel stocks: what does the saved September 4, 2026 snapshot show?
answer: In the week ending September 4, 2026, the master's notes mark crude oil (Strategic Petroleum Reserve), motor gasoline and distillate fuel as lower or tighter than a year earlier and jet fuel and propane as above year-earlier levels; 6 fuels in all, each with its number below.

sections.title: Fuel by fuel, week ending September 4, 2026
sections.sub: M bbl means million barrels. Each note says what the number does and does not show.

items.label: Crude oil (commercial)
items.note: Weekly national stock is nearly flat year over year but does not prove regional or grade-specific availability

items.label: Crude oil (Strategic Petroleum Reserve)
items.note: Emergency government inventory is not commercial availability and is materially below the year-earlier level

items.label: Motor gasoline
items.note: National stock was lower year over year but built in the latest week and does not establish a local retail shortage

items.label: Distillate fuel
items.note: Real national tightness includes severe East Coast weakness but weekly stock is not proof of imminent physical stockout

items.label: Jet fuel
items.note: National stock above year-earlier level does not rule out airport or regional logistics constraints

items.label: Propane
items.note: National stock above year-earlier level does not establish winter regional deliverability

A national stock number does not show regional or local shortages.

The graphic registry labels its evidence September 9, 2026. The linked inventory analysis says the September 4 observations were released September 10 and accessed September 15. Those labels conflict; September 9 cannot be treated as a verified review of that later-released table. Original dates are retained pending owner reconciliation.
